timeledger

Auditable time accounting for evaluating detectors of events in long, continuous recordings.

Two monitors read the same 24-hour ECG. One skips four hard hours. Judged only on the hours it answered, it can beat the other monitor and still miss more atrial fibrillation (AF) over the day. It can even report the right number of AF minutes while flagging the wrong ones. timeledger keeps the reference, the input status and each detector’s answers in one table of non-overlapping time intervals, and every number it reports is computed from that table.

library(timeledger)
fx <- tl_fixture("acceptance")              # the 100-minute example
led <- tl_ledger(fx$records, fx$reference, fx$predictions, time_unit = "min")
m <- tl_match(led, policy = "one_to_one")
tl_get(tl_metrics(led, m), c("answer_coverage", "answered_sensitivity",
                             "full_capture", "episode_sensitivity"))
tl_explain(led, m, episode = "rec1:e002")   # the seconds behind a missed episode

What it keeps apart:

Situation Ledger state
Reference rhythm unknown reference = "unknown", left out of truth-based denominators
Monitor had no input response = "no_input", from an explicit observation table
Input available, detector declined response = "abstain", with its reason
Detector answered “no event” response = "negative"
No prediction row and no declared meaning response = "unknown" (never silently negative)

Main functions: tl_ledger(), tl_check(), tl_metrics(), tl_match() (one-to-one with exact dynamic programming, or any-overlap), tl_compare() (own, shared and full time), tl_bootstrap() (subject-level, paired), tl_trace() / tl_explain(), plot(); WFDB adapters read_wfdb_ann(), write_wfdb_ann(), wfdb_rhythm_intervals(), and wfdb_epicmp_af(), which reproduces the AF statistics of WFDB epicmp 10.7.0 (verified against the executable on 109 records under two detector policies; this is a compatibility mode, not a claim of standards compliance).

The package depends only on base R (graphics, stats, utils).

Citation

Menneni T (2026). timeledger: Auditable Time Accounting for Evaluating Continuous Event Detectors. Archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24489065.

Installation 

# development version (not yet on CRAN)
install.packages("timeledger_0.1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

Status

Version 0.1.0 is a first release. It has not yet been used by anyone other than its author. Bug reports and use cases are welcome via the issue tracker.

Data

inst/extdata contains the annotation files of record 04015 of the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database (Moody and Mark 1983), distributed by PhysioNet under the Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0. See data-raw/README.md.
